problem_statement: Write a program that counts the total number of vowels and consonants in a given sentence, ignoring spaces and special characters. Given Input: \"Loops are Fun!\" Expected Output: Vowels: 5, Consonants: 7.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.description: Evaluates if the algorithm accurately categorizes each alphabetic character as a vowel or consonant and correctly ignores non-alphabetic characters.
sub_criteria: The logic correctly identifies an alphabetic character as a vowel.
The logic correctly identifies an alphabetic character as a consonant.
The logic correctly ignores non-alphabetic characters (e.g., spaces, punctuation, numbers).
The comparison for vowels and consonants is case-insensitive.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.description: Evaluates whether all necessary parts of the algorithm are present, including input processing, counting mechanisms, and handling of various character types.
sub_criteria: The algorithm includes counters for both vowels and consonants.
The algorithm describes how to iterate through each character of the input sentence.
The algorithm describes how to accumulate the counts based on character type.
The algorithm addresses situations where the input sentence is empty or contains no alphabetic characters.

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.description: Evaluates how easy it is to understand the logical flow and purpose of each step in the pseudocode.
sub_criteria: The steps clearly describe the process of checking each character's type.
The names for variables and quantities (e.g., input sentence, current character, vowel count, consonant count) are clear and consistent.
The overall flow of the algorithm, from start to finish, is easy to understand.

dimensions.name: Efficiency
dimensions.description: Evaluates the algorithmic approach for avoiding unnecessary operations or redundant processing.
sub_criteria: The algorithm processes each character in the input sentence at most once to determine its type.
The algorithm avoids any redundant or unnecessary passes over the entire input sentence.
